messages.author: 2b9ec73e360bf803
messages.subject: INLA intermittently drops fixed effects
parts:
I'm running a number of large (~100,000 data points, 15+ hours on 60 cores) runs with continuous space-time GLMs. Occasionally (maybe 1 in 10 runs) the run completes, but has lost the fixed effects along the way. I.e. it fits a models with the random effects but states that no fixed effects were specified:

  Model contains 3 hyperparameters
  The model has no fixed effects and no intercept

However the fixed effects *are* specified, in both the formula and stack. This is stochastic - I can re-run an identical script with identical data and it will complete as expected the second time around.

Given the long run times and intermittency of the bug, it has taken a while to get any useful feedback. But I've attached a text file with part of the code to fit the model, most of the log generated with verbose = TRUE (copied from R console, will log properly in future) and some of the structure of the fitted model object. I've saved the model (which is >1GB with compression :\), so can get more details of this run if needs be.

Notice it's doing something with those covariates (lines 72, 106, 140 etc.)

I appreciate this isn't an easy one to diagnose from the information given, but any ideas or pointers to what sort of logging would help would be much appreciated!

Nick

Good to know it isn't just me!

I have working theory (discussed with Håvard on email) that it runs the model fine with fixed effects but silently fails when reading the estimated coefficients back in from a temporary datafile.

I am running models with verbose = TRUE and keep = TRUE so next time around I can (hopefully) check to see if the relevant file is written to disk, and whether it is just an intermittent failure reading from disk.

Hmmm... I do run everything using RStudio Server, but I'm not sure why that would affect this. Will see what I can figure out if/when this happens again.
